desc: Derive correct model: optimal = bubble values in decreasing order; answer = Σ_v (S(v-1) - S(r_v-1)), r_v = rank of pos[v] among pos[1..v]; verified on samples 1-3 and extra cases (reverse of 4 → 10, (3,2,4,1) → 7)
Establish lower-bound proof: charge each swap to its rightward mover; element v must make rightward swaps at boundaries ≥ j for each j in [r_v, v-1], and decreasing-order bubbling achieves it
Implement solve(): fast stdin read, pos array, Fenwick (count BIT over positions 1..N), loop v=1..N: r_v = bit.sum(pos[v]); ans += (v-1)*v//2 - (r_v-1)*r_v//2; bit.add(pos[v],1); print ans
Sanity-check implementation against samples mentally (expect 4, 6, 0) and confirm O(N log N), Python int handles ~1.3e15 answer
